children.title: Burgum Calls the Energy Transition an Ideological “Fantasy”
children.description_short: Interior Secretary Doug Burgum called the energy transition an ideological “fantasy” during February 2026 remarks.
children.description_medium: On February 12, 2026, Interior Secretary Doug Burgum described the energy transition as an ideological “fantasy” based on “incomplete data” during remarks at a Foundation for Defense of Democracies event. E&E News reported that he also questioned climate-science forecasts and discussed plans to expand domestic critical-mineral reserves. This card covers his reported remarks only.
children.description_long: On February 12, 2026, Interior Secretary Doug Burgum described the energy transition as an ideological “fantasy” based on “incomplete data” during remarks at a Foundation for Defense of Democracies event. E&E News reported that he cast doubt on widely accepted climate science and discussed plans to expand domestic critical-mineral reserves. The article also quotes him saying, “I come from a belief system that science is never settled,” and records his criticism of long-range climate forecasts. This card covers those reported remarks and does not treat them as a new regulation or as proof of a particular environmental outcome. The article separately reports that the Trump administration repealed the EPA endangerment finding on the same day; that was a distinct government action and is not included in this child record. The original July 14 date is replaced with the date of the contemporaneous report. The source provides journalistic attribution rather than an event recording, so the quotations are attributed to E&E News and have not been independently checked against audio or a transcript.

By Ian M. Stevenson | 02/12/2026 04:00 PM EST

Interior Secretary Doug Burgum cast doubt on climate science Thursday, the same day that the Trump administration rolled back foundational U.S. climate policy through its repeal of the endangerment finding.

Burgum called the energy transition an ideological “fantasy” that was based on “incomplete data” from models that track climate indicators during remarks at event held by the Foundation for Defense of Democracies, a think tank.

children.title: Interior Holds NPR-A Lease Sale With 187 Leases
children.description_short: Interior’s March 18, 2026 NPR-A sale resulted in 187 leases across about 1.3 million acres.
children.description_medium: On March 18, 2026, the Department of the Interior held an oil-and-gas lease sale in Alaska’s National Petroleum Reserve. Interior reported 187 leases covering about 1.3 million acres and described the sale as the reserve’s first since 2019. The Bureau of Land Management’s sale table lists $163,696,722.20 in high bids. The auction does not establish that all tracts will be developed or that environmental damage has occurred.
children.description_long: On March 18, 2026, the Department of the Interior held an oil-and-gas lease sale in Alaska’s National Petroleum Reserve. The department’s release says the sale resulted in 187 leases and was the first such sale in the reserve since 2019. It reports bids on 187 tracts covering 1,334,967 acres; the Bureau of Land Management’s sale table lists $163,696,722.20 in high bids. These are bids and awarded leases, not proof that every tract will be developed or that production or environmental damage has already occurred. Interior described the sale as the first in the reserve under the One Big Beautiful Bill Act. The stored July 14 date is replaced with the official event date. This child is limited to the March auction; Burgum’s February remarks, the supplied royalty-rate claim, and a separate November 2025 decision to reopen much of the reserve to leasing are excluded because they have different dates or lack support in this packet. The accessed sources do not detail lease terms, later development, or site-specific effects, so those outcomes remain unknown.

title: White House Press Secretary Says Temple-Rebuilding Talks Had Not Occurred
description_short: At a 2025 White House briefing, Karoline Leavitt said rebuilding the Holy Temple had not come up with Trump.
description_medium: At the October 23, 2025 White House briefing, reporter Jake Turx asked Press Secretary Karoline Leavitt whether rebuilding the Holy Temple in Jerusalem had come up in discussions with President Donald Trump. Turx linked his question to the new ballroom renderings. Leavitt said it had not. This card documents that exchange only; it does not establish a religious motive for the ballroom or a broader Temple-related policy.
description_long: At the October 23, 2025 White House briefing, reporter Jake Turx asked Press Secretary Karoline Leavitt whether rebuilding the Holy Temple in Jerusalem had come up in discussions with President Donald Trump. Turx introduced the question while referring to the new ballroom renderings and saying they had prompted the thought. Leavitt answered that the subject had not come up. This documented exchange is the narrower supported subject for the record. It confirms that a reporter made an association after seeing the renderings and that the press secretary denied prior discussion; it does not establish that Trump proposed or approved a Temple project, that the ballroom had a religious or messianic purpose, or that the administration coordinated with Third Temple organizations. The exchange also does not support the original record’s links to the Abraham Accords, Jared Kushner, Oracle, Larry Ellison, or surveillance technology, so those separate strands are removed. This was a question and answer, not an enacted policy or a finding about private conversations. The stored January 20 date is replaced with October 23, 2025, the date shown on the briefing transcript. The available reporting records Leavitt’s answer but cannot independently establish what may have been discussed privately.

The HHS Office of Population Affairs (OPA) awarded $2 million in one-time supplemental funding from the Public Health Prevention Fund to 11 Title X service grant recipients.

source_fact_map.fact: KFF reports that 16 of 86 Title X grantees received notice on March 31, 2025 that their year-four funding would be temporarily withheld.
source_fact_map.quote: On March 31, 2025, almost one in five (16 out of 86) of the current Title X grantees received notification that their year 4 funding of a 5-year project period would be temporarily withheld.
source_fact_map.source_excerpt: On March 31, 2025, almost one in five (16 out of 86) of the current Title X grantees received notification that their year 4 funding of a 5-year project period would be temporarily withheld. This funding freeze affects all 9 of the Planned Parenthood grantees, in addition to 7 other nonprofit grantees.

source_fact_map.fact: KFF estimates 879 clinics in 23 states were affected and up to 834,000 people might lose access if funds were not released.
source_fact_map.quote: KFF estimates that a total of 879 clinics (24% of all Title X clinics) in 23 states are affected by the funding freeze
source_fact_map.source_excerpt:
KFF estimates that a total of 879 clinics (24% of all Title X clinics) in 23 states are affected by the funding freeze (Table 1).

According to one estimate, up to 834,000 people may lose access to Title X-funded care if these funds are not released.

source_fact_map.fact: The KFF profile states Title X supports nearly 4,000 clinics and 2.8 million clients; it does not report the original entry's 1,600 forced closures or 4 million affected patients.
source_fact_map.quote: Federal support assists nearly 4,000 clinics across the country to provide services to 2.8 million clients
source_fact_map.source_excerpt: Title X provides federal funding to support clinics across the country to provide comprehensive family planning services to low-income and uninsured individuals. Federal support assists nearly 4,000 clinics across the country to provide services to 2.8 million clients in all 50 states, D.C. and U.S. territories.

source_fact_map.fact: The complaint filed by the National Family Planning & Reproductive Health Association alleged that HHS withheld $65.8 million from 16 grantees; this is a plaintiff allegation, not a court finding.
source_fact_map.quote: unlawfully withheld $65.8 million in Title X grants for federally funded family planning services from sixteen Title X grantees
source_fact_map.source_excerpt:
COMPLAINT FOR DECLARATORY AND INJUNCTIVE RELIEF (Challenge to unlawful withholding of Title X funds)

INTRODUCTION

The United States Department of Health and Human Services (“HHS” or “the Agency”) has unlawfully withheld $65.8 million in Title X grants for federally funded family planning services from sixteen Title X grantees.

source_fact_map.quote: On March 31, 2025, 16 grantees received notice that the Trump administration was “temporarily withholding” funding for 22 of their Title X grants for fiscal year 2025, effective the following day.
source_fact_map.source_excerpt: On March 31, 2025, 16 grantees received notice that the Trump administration was “temporarily withholding” funding for 22 of their Title X grants for fiscal year 2025, effective the following day. (These grants represent nearly a quarter of the 86 Title X service grants awarded for FY2024.)

counterpart_comparison.comparison: Full card describes the same March 31 temporary Title X freeze affecting 16 of 86 grantees and cites KFF's 879-clinic/834,000-patient estimates. It is a distinct later event from the unsupported February all-program termination asserted by entry-6821; if the March event is discussed, entry-4766 is the existing record.
Full card describes the March 31 notice to nine Planned Parenthood affiliates, a narrower group in the same later freeze. It does not establish a February termination of all federal programs.

uncertainties: The eventual duration and final disposition of the March 31 temporary withholding are not established by the accessed sources.
KFF clinic and patient figures are estimates; the NFPRHA filing's different figures are allegations, not court findings.
No accessed source establishes that the original 1,600 centers were forced to close or that 4 million people lost access because of a February action.
This terminal is an exclusion candidate for the unsupported February claim; it does not propose replacing it with or merging it into the separate March event.

impact_proposal.confidence_reason: The alleged February-wide termination is contradicted by the available official directory and narrower dated coverage; the claimed harm quantities are not supported.
impact_proposal.rationale: No defensible event matching the original card remains. The documented March 31 temporary withholding is a separate event and already has a related catalog record, so its impacts should not be scored under this entry.
